verdict.rationale: The evidence includes the project's public GitHub repository (github.com/mozilla-ai/llamafile), so the source appears readable. Mozilla.ai also lists llamafile under 'open-tools', but no evidence item names an open-source license for llamafile's code. The only 'open-source' mention refers to the LLMs users deploy, not llamafile itself. Missing for 10: an explicit license statement (e.g., Apache/MIT) for llamafile's source, documentation pointing to the source tree or build-from-source path, and independent corroboration of its open licensing.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can read the product's source under an open license

citations.quote: collapses all the complexity of LLMs down to a single-file executable (called a "llamafile") that runs locally on most operating systems and CPU architectures, with no installation.
llamafile also includes whisperfile, a single-file speech-to-text tool built on whisper.cpp and the same Cosmopolitan packaging.
